2026-08-13T12:35:01.8749503Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8750081Z 
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8750410Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8750893Z 
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8751293Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8751784Z 
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8753322Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8755003Z >
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8757268Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8759643Z >
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8760741Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8761503Z 
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8761678Z ### How to Use
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8761905Z 
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8762619Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8763769Z 
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8763949Z ```bash
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8764511Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8765232Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8765833Z ```
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8766036Z 
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8766290Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8767202Z ```bash
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8767741Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8768517Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8769342Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8770282Z ```
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8770567Z 
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8771226Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8772079Z ```bash
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8772627Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8773298Z ```
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8773501Z 
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8773815Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8774569Z ```bash
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8775090Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8775941Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8776642Z ```
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8776839Z 
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8777105Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8777519Z 
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8778923Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8780703Z 
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8780882Z ```bash
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8781316Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8782157Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8782961Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8783273Z 
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8783747Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8784741Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8785552Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8786014Z ```
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8786209Z 
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8786961Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8787861Z 
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8788029Z ```bash
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8788690Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8789559Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8790470Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8790908Z 
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8791304Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8792103Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8793049Z ```
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8793259Z 
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8793463Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8794284Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8795239Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8796191Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8797185Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8798293Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8798829Z 
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8798995Z ### Notes
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8799213Z 
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8800023Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8801436Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8802666Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8803902Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8805082Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8806193Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8807137Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-13T12:35:01.8807814Z </mcp-clis>
